title: Challenge: grant least-privilege access with RBAC
intro: User john.doe needs to read pods in the 'rbac-demo' namespace, and nothing more. You'll prove it's denied, grant exactly that with a Role + RoleBinding, and prove it now works. (Commands checked; output illustrative.)

steps.instruction: First, confirm john.doe@example.com currently CANNOT list pods in rbac-demo.
steps.fail: Use kubectl auth can-i with --namespace=rbac-demo and --as=john.doe@example.com.

steps.instruction: Create a Role named 'pod-reader' in rbac-demo allowing get/list/watch on pods.
Bind that Role to john.doe with a RoleBinding named 'pod-reader-binding'.
Now check again, can john.doe list pods in rbac-demo?
steps.success: yes  ✓, access granted, scoped to exactly pods in rbac-demo and nothing else
steps.fail: Re-run the same auth can-i check.

done: Solved! That's RBAC: a Role says WHAT (verbs on resources), a RoleBinding says WHO. Least privilege = grant the smallest Role that does the job, nothing wider.
